gloss: seek, inquire of, consult; require, demand; investigate; care for; study
summary: To seek with purpose and keep returning to what is sought: to go and inquire of God, a prophet, or (forbidden) the dead and other gods; to seek Yahweh himself in worship and obedience, the seeking that is answered with finding and life (Deu 4:29; Amo 5:4); to require back what is owed, above all blood; to search out a matter; to look after and care for; and to search out Yahweh's law and works. The niphal is to be sought or inquired of, of Yahweh, who refuses those who come with idols in their heart; the noun מִדְרָשׁ is a written study or record. Arabic darasa (tread out by passing over again and again; read over and study; train) and the Aramaic and Syriac verb (interpret; question, dispute; train) show the root's repeated, searching application.

words.gloss: seek, inquire of; seek (God) in worship; require; investigate; care for; study
words.summary: About 165 times, nearly all qal. It is set beside בִּקֵּשׁ “search for” (Deu 4:29; Psa 105:4; Jer 29:13; Zep 1:6), שָׁאַל “ask” (Deu 13:15; Isa 65:1) and חָקַר “search out” (Deu 13:15), and against עָזַב “abandon” (2Ch 15:2; 1Ch 28:9; Psa 9:11). Where בִּקֵּשׁ is to look for what is missing, דָּרַשׁ is to go to someone or something for an answer, or to keep after it with care: the land Yahweh “seeks” is the land his eyes are always on (Deu 11:12).

stems.gloss: inquire of, consult; seek (God) in worship; require, demand; investigate; care for; seek out, study

senses.gloss: inquire of, consult (God, a prophet; the dead, other gods)
senses.definition: To go to God, his prophet or seer, or to a medium, the dead or a foreign god, to ask for a word or an answer about what to do or what will happen. Inquiring of the dead and of other gods is forbidden.

evidence.note: “Formerly in Israel, when a man went לִדְרוֹשׁ אֱלֹהִים, he said, Come, let us go to the seer”: inquiring of God is going to his prophet.
Rebekah, troubled by the children struggling within her, “went to inquire of Yahweh”, and Yahweh answered her (25:23).
“The people come to me to inquire of God.”
“There is yet one man by whom to inquire of Yahweh, Micaiah son of Imlah.”
Josiah on finding the book: “Go, inquire of Yahweh for me and for the people.”
“Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?”
“When they say to you, Inquire of the mediums … should not a people inquire of its God? For the living, to the dead?”
Among the forbidden practices, “one who inquires of the dead (דֹרֵשׁ אֶל־הַמֵּתִים)”.
Saul died for consulting a medium “to inquire”, “and he did not inquire of Yahweh”.
Elders came “to inquire of Yahweh” and sat before Ezekiel.
“Inquire of Yahweh for us, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us.”
The envoys of Babylon came “to inquire about the sign that had been in the land”.

senses.gloss: seek (Yahweh, or another god) in worship and obedience
senses.definition: To turn to Yahweh as one's God, to look to him, pray to him and keep his ways; the opposite of abandoning him. It is done with the whole heart, and he is found by those who seek him so. The same verb is used of seeking other gods, which is forbidden.

evidence.note: “You will search for (וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם) Yahweh your God and will find him, כִּי תִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ with all your heart and with all your soul.”
“דִּרְשׁוּנִי וִחְיוּ”: seek me and live.
“Do not seek Bethel … Seek Yahweh and live”: seeking Yahweh set against seeking the shrines.
“If you seek him he will be found by you, but if you abandon him he will abandon you.”
“Yahweh searches (דּוֹרֵשׁ) all hearts … if you seek him he will be found by you, but if you abandon him he will reject you for ever.”
Yahweh looks down “to see if there is one who understands, דֹּרֵשׁ אֶת־אֱלֹהִים”; none is found (14:3). Quoted at Rom 3:11.
“There is none who seeks (ἐκζητῶν) God”, from Psa 14:2; 53:3.
“Seek Yahweh and his strength; search for (בַּקְּשׁוּ) his face continually.”
“Seek Yahweh while he may be found; call on him while he is near.”
“You will search for me and find me, when you seek me with all your heart.”
“Those who turn back from following Yahweh, who have not searched for Yahweh nor sought him.”
“The wicked in his pride does not seek; all his thoughts are, There is no God.”
“You have not abandoned those who seek you, Yahweh.”
“I sought Yahweh, and he answered me.”
A covenant “to seek Yahweh the God of their fathers with all their heart”.
Rehoboam “did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek Yahweh”.
“It is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.”
“The root of Jesse … to him the nations shall seek”; Rom 15:12 quotes the verse in the Septuagint's words.
“Day by day they seek me and delight to know my ways”, yet without righteousness: seeking that is only outward.
God “is a rewarder of those who seek him (τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτόν)”.
“Lest you inquire about their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods?”
The host of heaven “which they loved and served, after which they walked, which they sought, and which they worshipped”.

senses.definition: To seek back from someone what is owed: the life for shed blood, a vow, a duty, offerings; to hold to account. God is the one who requires.

evidence.note: “Your blood for your lives אֶדְרֹשׁ; from the hand of every beast אֶדְרְשֶׁנּוּ … from the hand of man I will require the life of man.”
“When you vow a vow … do not delay to pay it, for Yahweh your God will surely require it of you.”
“Whoever will not listen to my words which he speaks in my name, I will require it of him”; Act 3:23 applies the verse to Jesus.
“What does Yahweh require of you, but to do justice, to love kindness and to walk humbly with your God?”
“His blood I will require at the watchman's hand.”
“I am against the shepherds, and I will require my flock at their hand.”
“He who requires blood (דֹרֵשׁ דָּמִים) remembers them.”
The wicked says in his heart, “You will not require it.”
Zechariah son of Jehoiada, stoned in the court of the house of Yahweh, said as he died, “May Yahweh see and require (וְיִדְרֹשׁ).”
“The blood of all the prophets … may be required (ἐκζητηθῇ) of this generation, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah.”
“There I will require your offerings and the first of your gifts.”
“Why have you not required of the Levites to bring in the tax of Moses?”

senses.gloss: inquire into, investigate, search out (a matter)
senses.definition: To look into a matter thoroughly to find the truth of it, as a judge does; to search for something until it is found.

evidence.note: “וְדָרַשְׁתָּ וְחָקַרְתָּ וְשָׁאַלְתָּ הֵיטֵב, and behold, it is true”: inquire, search out, ask well.
“The judges shall inquire diligently, and behold, the witness is a false witness.”
“You shall inquire diligently, and behold, it is true.”
“Who has done this thing? וַיִּדְרְשׁוּ וַיְבַקְשׁוּ, and they said, Gideon.”
David sent and inquired about the woman.
Moses “diligently sought (דָּרֹשׁ דָּרַשׁ)” the goat of the sin offering, and it had been burnt.
“That you seek out my iniquity and search for my sin.”
“Seek out his wickedness until you find none.”
They sat down “to examine the matter”.
“I gave my heart לִדְרוֹשׁ וְלָתוּר in wisdom”: to seek and explore.
The stray animal is kept “until your brother seeks it”.
The wild donkey “searches after every green thing”.

senses.gloss: look after, care for; seek the good (or harm) of
senses.definition: To keep one's attention on someone or something for its good: Yahweh caring for his land and seeking out his scattered flock, the exiles seeking the peace of Babylon; or the reverse, seeking someone's harm. Its absence is neglect: “no one seeks her”.

evidence.note: “A land which Yahweh your God דֹּרֵשׁ אֹתָהּ; the eyes of Yahweh your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to its end.”
“I myself will seek my flock and look after them (וּבִקַּרְתִּים)”; contrast 34:6, “there is none who seeks and none who searches”.
“They have called you an outcast: She is Zion, no one seeks her (דֹּרֵשׁ אֵין לָהּ)”, and Yahweh will heal her.
Zion shall be called “דְרוּשָׁה, a city not forsaken”.
“There is no one who cares for my soul.”
“Seek the peace of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to Yahweh for it.”
Mordecai, “seeking the good of his people”.
“You shall not seek their peace or their good all your days.”
“This man does not seek the peace of this people, but their harm.”
“Those who seek my hurt speak of ruin.”
“Whoever seeks evil, it will come to him.”
The capable wife “seeks wool and flax”.
“Let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul.”

senses.gloss: seek out, study (Yahweh's law, works, justice)
senses.definition: To give oneself to searching out Yahweh's law, commandments and works, so as to know and do them; to pursue justice.

evidence.note: “Ezra set his heart לִדְרוֹשׁ אֶת־תּוֹרַת יְהוָה, and to do it, and to teach statute and judgment in Israel.”
“Great are the works of Yahweh, דְּרוּשִׁים by all who delight in them”: searched out, studied.
“Seek out of the book of Yahweh and read.”
“I will walk at liberty, for I have sought your precepts.”
“Salvation is far from the wicked, for they do not seek your statutes.”
“Keep and seek out all the commandments of Yahweh your God, that you may possess this good land.”
“Learn to do good, seek justice.”
A judge “seeking justice and swift in righteousness”.

stems.gloss: be inquired of, let oneself be sought (of Yahweh); be required; be searched out

senses.gloss: be inquired of, let oneself be sought
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to let himself be consulted and found, or to refuse it to those whose hearts are set on idols.

evidence.note: “These men have set up their idols in their heart … הַאִדָּרֹשׁ אִדָּרֵשׁ לָהֶם?”: should I let myself be inquired of by them at all?
“As I live, I will not be inquired of by you.”
“This also I will let the house of Israel ask of me, to do it for them: I will increase them like a flock.”
“נִדְרַשְׁתִּי by those who did not ask; I was found by those who did not seek me.”
Paul quotes Isa 65:1 of the nations: “I was found by those who did not seek me.”

senses.definition: Of shed blood: to be required back, called to account.

evidence.note: Reuben: “Did I not say, Do not sin against the boy? … now his blood, behold, נִדְרָשׁ.”

senses.definition: Of men in the records: to be searched for and found.

evidence.note: “In the fortieth year of David's reign they were searched out, and mighty men were found among them at Jazer.”

evidence.locator: Gen.9.5, אֶדְרֹשׁ → ἐκζητήσω; Deu.4.29 → ἐκζητήσητε; Psa.14.2, דֹּרֵשׁ → ἐκζητῶν; Amo.5.4 → ἐκζητήσατε; Mic.6.8 → ἐκζητεῖ; Ezk.34.11 → ἐκζητήσω; ἐκζητέω renders דָּרַשׁ ×46

evidence.note: “There is none who seeks God (ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν)”: the Septuagint's word at Psa 14:2.
“That the blood of all the prophets … ἐκζητηθῇ from this generation”: the requiring of blood of Gen 9:5 and 2Ch 24:22.
“A rewarder of those who seek him out.”

evidence.locator: Ezr.7.10, לִדְרוֹשׁ → ζητῆσαι; Lev.10.16 → ζητῶν; ζητέω renders דָּרַשׁ ×36

evidence.note: “Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
Isa 65:1 in the Septuagint's words: “I became manifest to those who did not ask for me (ἐπερωτῶσιν).”

parallels.note: “Search for”: the commonest partner, in seeking Yahweh and in searching out a matter.

opposites.note: “Abandon”: those who seek Yahweh are not abandoned; those who abandon him are.

phrases.gloss: seek Yahweh: inquire of him, or turn to him in worship
set the heart to seek (Yahweh, his law)
require blood: call the shedder to account

words.summary: Twice, both in Chronicles, naming a written source: what was searched out and set down. Only two uses, both naming a book, so the sense rests on the verb's “seek out, study” more than on its own verses.

senses.definition: A written work that searches out and sets down the acts of kings, cited by the Chronicler as his source.

evidence.note: “The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his words, are written בְּמִדְרַשׁ of the prophet Iddo.”
Joash's sons, the oracles against him and the rebuilding of the house of God “are written in the מִדְרַשׁ of the book of the kings”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb of the root: in the peal, to question one another and dispute, for συζητέω and διαλέγομαι; in the pael, to train or exercise, for γυμνάζω. The dispute is the Hebrew's inquiry turned into argument; the training answers Arabic darasa, to break in a camel and to read over again and again.

senses.definition: To question and argue with others, of the scribes with the disciples, the synagogue of the Freedmen with Stephen, Paul with Jews, Greeks and philosophers.

evidence.note: The scribes “כַּדֿ דָּרשִינ עַמהֻונ”: disputing with them (συζητοῦντας); Jesus asks, “What are you disputing with them?” (9:16).
A scribe heard them “disputing” and asked which commandment is first.
Men of the synagogue of the Freedmen “ודָֿרשִינ ה_וַו עַמ אֵסטֵפַֿנָוס”.
Paul “ודָֿרֵש ה_וָא” with the Greek-speaking Jews.
Epicurean and Stoic philosophers “disputed with him”.
Apollos “powerfully disputed (דָּרֵש ה_וָא) against the Jews before the crowds, showing from the scriptures that Jesus is the Messiah”.
The Jews went out, “and they disputed much among themselves”.

senses.definition: To train by practice, the self in godliness, the senses to discern good and evil, or (of false teachers) a heart in covetousness; passive participle, trained, instructed.

evidence.note: “ודַֿרֵש נַפֿשָכֿ in godliness”: train yourself (γύμναζε).
Solid food is for the mature, “who because they are trained (דַּמדַֿרשִינ) have their senses exercised to distinguish good and evil”.
“A heart trained (דַּמדַֿרַש) in covetousness.”
“In everything and in all things מדַֿרַש א_נָא”: I have been trained, both to be full and to be hungry (μεμύημαι).

senses.definition: Passive of the pael: to be trained by discipline.

evidence.note: Discipline yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness “to those who אֵתּדַּרַשו by it” (γεγυμνασμένοις).

senses.definition: Argument for its own sake, the sickness of a proud teacher.

evidence.note: He is proud, knowing nothing, “but sick בַּדֿרָשָא and in disputes about words” (ζητήσεις).

senses.definition: One skilled in argument, set beside the wise man and the scribe.

evidence.note: “Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the דָּרֻושָא of this world?” (συζητητής).

senses.definition: Training of the body, set against godliness, which profits in all things.

evidence.note: “דֻּורָשָא of the body profits a little, but godliness profits in all things, having the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come” (γυμνασία).

cognates.gloss: (of wind) efface by passing over again and again; tread out, thresh (grain); break in, train (a she-camel); read over repeatedly, study; (dursa) training, discipline; (midrās) one who studies the books of the Jews
cognates.note: The common thread is going over the same thing again and again: treading, breaking in, reading over. This answers the Hebrew's persistent seeking, its “study” of Yahweh's law and works (Ezr 7:10; Psa 111:2), and the Syriac pael “train”. Arabic s answers Hebrew שׁ as š (Arabic would show ث for ṯ; the brief found nothing under درث). The Wiktionary etymology reports Geiger's view that the Qur'an's use for interpreting scripture is borrowed from Hebrew; the treading and training senses are native Arabic.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 870–871, art. درس, دَرَسَ (n12416)
evidence.note: “The wind effaced … it, by repeatedly passing over it … He trod, or thrashed, the wheat … He broke, or trained, the she-camel … the primary signification of مُدَارَسَةٌ is the breaking, or training … and returning time after time to a thing … He read the book … he read it repeatedly, [or studied it,] in order to remember it.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 871, art. درس, دُرْسَةٌ (n12423)
evidence.note: “Training, or discipline.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 871, art. درس, مِدْرَاسٌ (n12432)
evidence.note: “One who reads, or reads repeatedly, or studies, the books of the Jews.”
Glosses erase, thresh, study; reports Geiger's view of the Qur'anic sense as a semantic loan from Hebrew דָּרַשׁ.

cognates.gloss: interpret, expound (a verse); lecture, teach; (ithpeel) be interpreted
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the searching out of scripture, the sense of Ezr 7:10 and of מִדְרָשׁ. Its Hebrew of the same period also has “examine, question”.

evidence.locator: D01130 s.v. דְּרַשׁ (ch.), citing Targ. Jud. V, 9; Succ. 51b (they found a verse and interpreted it); Ber. 28a (lecture); Ber. 63a (Ithpe., be interpreted)
D01129 s.v. דָּרַשׁ, sense “to examine, question”; 1) to expound, interpret; 2) to teach, lecture

cognates.gloss: train; debate, argue, question, dispute; disputation; disputer; exercise
cognates.note: The Syriac of the Peshitta, given above as words of the entry with their verses: questioning that becomes dispute, and training by practice.

evidence.locator: root 481 DRW; lexemes 765 DRW (train; debate; argue; question; dispute), 766 DRWA (disputation), 764 DROWA (disputer), 763 DORWA (exercise)

cognates.gloss: expound, comment on (a reading) in a homily; compose (books, sacred discourses); (dərsān) homily, treatise
cognates.note: Ge'ez church vocabulary, close to Jewish Aramaic “expound” and to מִדְרָשׁ; it may have come in through Aramaic with the scriptures rather than by descent.

evidence.locator: col. 1093–1094, art. ደረሰ, “librum vel lectionem … tractare exegetice vel homiletice … commentari … conscribere, componere libros, orationes sacras”; ድርሳን “tractatus, dissertatio … homilia”

cognates.note: Three uncertain attestations; the trampling would answer Arabic darasa “tread out”, but Akkadian š does not show which older sound stands behind ש, and the meaning does not reach the Hebrew's seeking.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh says to Israel, “Seek me and live … seek Yahweh and live” (Amo 5:4, 6), and the seeking is answered: “you will find him, when you seek him with all your heart and all your soul” (Deu 4:29; Jer 29:13); “if you seek him he will be found by you, but if you abandon him he will abandon you” (2Ch 15:2; 1Ch 28:9). It has a time: “seek Yahweh while he may be found” (Isa 55:6), “it is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes and rains righteousness on you” (Hos 10:12). Left to themselves men do not seek: Yahweh looked for one who seeks God and found none (Psa 14:2–3), which Paul applies to Jew and Gentile alike (Rom 3:11), and Yahweh says he was found by a nation that did not seek him (Isa 65:1; Rom 10:20). “He who comes to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him” (Heb 11:6). From the verses: life is not something man already has but what Yahweh gives to those who seek him, and seeking him means turning to him with the whole heart while he may be found.

The law forbids “one who inquires of the dead” among the practices of the nations (Deu 18:10–12), and Isaiah asks, “Should not a people inquire of its God? For the living, to the dead?” (Isa 8:19), sending them “to the law and to the testimony” (Isa 8:20). Saul died for consulting a medium “to inquire, and he did not inquire of Yahweh” (1Ch 10:13–14). Scripture says why the dead cannot be asked: “the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing” (Ecc 9:5); “there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in the grave” (Ecc 9:10); man's breath goes out, he returns to his earth, “in that very day his thoughts perish” (Psa 146:4). From the verses: the dead have no knowledge to give, and to inquire of them is to turn from the living God who answers.

After the flood God said, “your blood for your lives I will require … from the hand of man I will require the life of man”, “for in the image of God he made man” (Gen 9:5–6). Joseph's brothers knew his blood was being required of them (Gen 42:22), and the psalmist calls Yahweh “he who requires blood” (Psa 9:13). Zechariah son of Jehoiada, stoned in the court of the house of Yahweh, said as he died, “May Yahweh see and require” (2Ch 24:20–22). Jesus took up his words: the blood of all the prophets, “from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house … shall be required of this generation” (Luk 11:50–51; Mat 23:35–36), and said of the temple, “there shall not be left here one stone upon another” (Mat 24:2), when Jerusalem would be surrounded by armies in “days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled” (Luk 21:20–22). From the verses: Yahweh requires shed blood of those who shed it, and the blood of the prophets was required of that generation when Jerusalem and its temple were destroyed in AD 70.

note: Left out: דַּרְיוֹשׁ (d.ch.ag), Darius, which BDB cross-refers here but is a Persian royal name (Old Persian Dārayavauš), not this root; no name file. No personal name is formed from דרש in TIPNR. No Biblical Aramaic word of the root. The Peshitta words are from SEDRA's BFBS text (root 481); the brief's “Peshitta cognate root” lists them. Open: (1) whether Arabic darasa “read, study” is native or, as some argue for the Qur'anic sense, a loan from Jewish usage; its treading and camel-training senses look native, and Syriac pael “train” matches them, so it is kept as a cognate with ש = š. (2) The Ge'ez darasa may be borrowed from Aramaic; marked possible. (3) Act 15:17's “that the rest of men may seek the Lord (ἐκζητήσωσιν)” follows a Septuagint reading of Amo 9:12 as יִדְרְשׁוּ where the Hebrew has יִירְשׁוּ “possess”; not cited as a use of the root. (4) Rom 15:12 quotes Isa 11:10 in the Septuagint's “in him shall the nations hope (ἐλπιοῦσιν)” for יִדְרֹשׁוּ. (5) The brief's niphal at 1Ch 26:31 is the only use of “be searched out”. Mandaic drš (Drower–Macuch) not consulted.
